node-1.label: 4-day history of progressive vesiculopustular eruption of the anterior neck and chin

node-2.label: Patient denied symptoms of pruritus, burning, or fever at time of presentation; had not received smallpox vaccination but had engaged in simulated unarmed combat with individuals who had recently been vaccinated

node-3.label: Physical examination revealed more than 2 dozen monomorphic, broad-based folliculocentric pustules with central umbilication, overlying serum crust, and surrounding erythema and edema of the anterior neck, chin, and inferior cheeks

node-4.label: During hospitalization, the patient developed fevers to 39°C, progressive edema of the face, and anterior cervical lymphadenopathy

node-5.label: Medical history was noncontributory, and the patient was not taking any medications

why.why: PCR detected vaccinia virus DNA, electron microscopy showed viral particles within Guarnieri bodies, and histopathology demonstrated Guarnieri bodies and viral inclusions. These expert-identified findings are core confirmatory evidence, and together with vaccinee exposure, no prior smallpox vaccination, and systemic symptoms (fever, facial edema, cervical lymphadenopathy) confirm vaccinia/orthopoxvirus infection. Confidence raised from 0.8 to 0.98; a small residual uncertainty remains because viral culture and paired serology are not yet available.

PCR detection of vaccinia virus DNA, electron microscopy demonstrating viral particles, and histopathology showing Guarnieri bodies directly exclude bacterial folliculitis/soft tissue infection. The folliculocentric pustules with central umbilication and vaccinee exposure also point to vaccinia rather than bacterial infection. Confidence reduced from 0.1 to 0.01.

PCR confirms vaccinia virus, and electron microscopy/histopathology show viral particles and Guarnieri bodies, which are not features of herpes simplex; expert analyses explicitly state that herpes simplex is excluded. Absence of pruritus/burning and known vaccinee contact further support vaccinia. Confidence reduced from 0.05 to 0.01.

Confirmed vaccinia/orthopoxvirus infection by PCR, electron microscopy, and histopathology, together with no medication use and absence of pruritus/burning, makes drug-related pustular eruption (AGEP) extremely unlikely. Confidence reduced from 0.05 to 0.01.
